exercise1.prompt: Define introduce() and call it twice

cases.name: two calls, so at least two lines of output

hiddenCases.name: introduce is defined and then called
hiddenCases.describe: a function named introduce, and a line that calls it

hiddenCases.name: the same output appears a second time
hiddenCases.describe: a repeated line, which is what a second call to the same function produces

exercise1.hint: Defining a function and running it are two separate things. Read your program from the top and ask which lines Python actually executes, and how many times.

exercise2.prompt: Define display_info() with three print statements and call it once

cases.name: three pieces of information, so three lines

hiddenCases.name: the three prints live inside display_info, which is then called
hiddenCases.describe: a function named display_info, and a line that calls it

exercise2.hint: Three prints one after another do produce three lines, but that is not what was asked. Check that the prints are indented under the def and that something calls the function.

questions.prompt: Which keyword begins a function definition?
questions.explain: Python uses def, followed by the name, the parentheses and a colon.

questions.prompt: You define a function but never call it. What happens?
choices: The body runs once, at the def line
The body runs when the program ends
questions.explain: A def only tells Python what the function does. The body waits until something calls it, which is why a program with a defined but uncalled function prints nothing.

questions.prompt: Put these lines in order so the program prints an introduction.
questions.explain: The def comes first, the indented body belongs to it, and the call sits back at the left margin so it is not part of the function it is calling.

questions.prompt: A function is run by writing its name followed by ___
questions.explain: The parentheses are what turn a name into a call. Writing introduce on its own just mentions the function; introduce() runs it.
